title: SRE: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning & Runbook Standards
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard approach for defining and operating Service Level Objectives (SLOs), managing error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, and runbook format. The goal is consistent, measurable reliability guarantees across our customer-facing inference services and internal platform components while providing clear oncall procedures and tooling guidance for SREs and service owners.

Scope:

- Applies to all services in the inference control plane and data path including inference-api, model-router, batcher, kv-cache, autoscaler, and console-backend.
- Does not replace product-level SLAs (legal contracts); SLAs should map to SLOs defined here.

Principles:

1. Measurable: every SLO must be backed by a clear metric, a dataset, and a query used to compute the SLO.
2. Owner-defined: product/service owners propose SLO targets; SRE validates observability and operational readiness.
3. Error-budget-driven operations: error budgets are used to guide rollouts, throttling, and remediation prioritization.
4. Automation first: automated mitigation, alerting, and capacity scaling preferred over manual play.

SLO taxonomy and example definitions:

We use two primary SLO types: Availability (correctness) and Latency (performance). A third optional type is Resource SLO (capacity constraints).

Example canonical SLO table (apply per service and per route when relevant):

| SLO name | Metric (datasource) | Window | Target | Evaluation query (example) | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| inference-api availability | successful_requests / total_requests (Prometheus, service:inference-api, status!~"5..") | 30d | 99.95% | sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\"}[30d])) - sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\",status=~\"5..\"}[30d])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\"}[30d])) | inference-api team | Exclude planned maintenance windows (see maintenance schedule). |
| generation latency (p95) | request_duration_seconds_bucket (Prometheus, route: /v1/generate) | 30d | <= 300ms | histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=\"/v1/generate\",job=\"inference-api\"}[30d])) by (le)) | inference-api team | Measure only successful requests.
| kv-cache miss rate | cache_miss_total / cache_request_total | 30d | <= 5% | increase(cache_miss_total[30d]) / increase(cache_request_total[30d]) | runtime team | High miss rate increases token cost.

SLO ownership and onboarding checklist:

- Service owner defines proposed SLO names, metrics, queries, and targets.
- SRE validates metric cardinality, cardinality cost, and feasibility of the query.
- Ensure dashboards and alerts exist for the SLO (see Operational Tooling).
- Add SLO to central SLO registry (git repo: infrastructure/slo-registry).
- Define error budget policy and rollout controls (canary limits, auto-block rules).

Error budget policy and operational playbook:

- Error budget = 1 - SLO. Example: 99.95% monthly availability -> error budget = 0.05% of minutes in 30 days (~21.6 minutes).
- We compute both rolling 30-day and calendar-month error budgets and track burn rate.
- Burn rate thresholds and operational responses (applies per SLO):
  - Normal: burn_rate <= 1 — no immediate action.
  - Elevated: burn_rate > 1 and <= 5 — inform owners, freeze risky changes, increase monitoring.
  - Critical: burn_rate > 5 — initiate mitigation runbook, rollback recent deploys, route traffic to fallback variants, restrict non-essential releases.

- Release gating: any canary rollout that consumes more than 10% of the monthly error budget in its first hour must be automatically aborted.
- Enforcement: PagerDuty and a Slack incident channel are created automatically when critical burn rate triggers occur.

Capacity planning and scaling standards:

Guidelines:
- Plan for observed peak + 25% headroom for typical production services; critical datapaths (inference-api, model-router) require 2x headroom for planned events (model launches).
- Capacity plans must include GPU pool sizing, autoscaling policy (`min_replicas`, `max_replicas`, target_cpu/gpu_utilization`), and cold-start latency budget.
- Use historical telemetry (90d) for baseline, then apply growth assumptions (quarterly).
- Document burst strategies: pre-warming, surge autoscale, and cross-region fallback.

Capacity plan template (text fields to include in repo):
- Service: inference-api
- Owner: inference-api team
- Baseline 90d peak qps: 48k requests/min
- Required throughput per GPU: 600 requests/min
- Calculated GPUs required at peak: ceiling(48k/600) = 80 GPUs
- Headroom factor: 1.25 -> target pool size: 100 GPUs
- Autoscaling policy: min=40, max=150, scale-out threshold = 70% GPU util, scale-in cooldown = 5m
- Runbook references: GPU capacity runbooks, node replacement playbook

Reliability initiatives and tech debt prioritization:

- Track reliability improvement work in a dedicated backlog board (label: reliability-initiative).
- Prioritize initiatives that materially reduce error budget burn or reduce blast radius of failures. Typical categories: retries and idempotency, graceful degradation (usage of smaller model fallback), caching improvements, cross-region failover, and observability gaps.
- Quarterly reliability hack weeks: focused sprints to fix high-impact flakiness. Each initiative must include an expected reduction in error budget minutes and a measured pre/post test.

Incident review standards and postmortem requirements:

- Every Sev 2/1 incident requires a postmortem within 7 days and a 1:1 review with SRE manager. Sev 3 may require a lightweight incident review based on impact threshold.
- Postmortem template (must be stored in incident-log repo and linked to confluence):
  - Title, incident id, severity, start/end time, customer impact summary
  - Timeline of events (UTC), detection method, and key decisions
  - Root cause analysis (tech root cause + organizational factors)
  - Action items (owner, due date, verification method)
  - Error budget impact and reliability metric deltas
  - Postmortem reviewer signoffs

- Action item policy: each Sev 1/2 must have at least two actionable items assigned and one must be to improve monitoring/alerting. Items must be tracked to completion with verification.

Runbook standards and templates:

- All runbooks live in github: infrastructure/runbooks/<service>-runbook.md and must be linked from the SLO registry entry.
- Runbooks must be human-readable, actionable, and include the following sections:
  - Symptom checklist (how will this appear in dashboards/alerts)
  - Impact assessment (how to tell if customers are impacted)
  - Quick mitigations (commands, immediate rollback steps, traffic routing)
  - Full remediation steps (detailed technical steps)
  - Escalation path and contacts
  - Post-incident verification and follow-up tasks

Sample runbook excerpt: High error rate on inference-api

1) Symptom:
   - SLO alert: inference-api availability critical (burn_rate > 5).
   - Grafana: 5xx spike from 00:12 UTC.
   - PagerDuty pager triggered for inference-api primary oncall.
2) Immediate mitigation (first 10 minutes):
   - Step 1: Acknowledge the PagerDuty incident.
   - Step 2: Check recent deploys: `git log --since=1h --oneline infra/deploys/inference-api` and `kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-api -n prod`. If a deploy finished within the last 15 minutes, rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-api -n prod`.
   - Step 3: If rollback is not possible or ineffective, scale up the model-router and batcher pools by 25%: `kubectl scale deployment/model-router --replicas=<current*1.25> -n prod` and `kubectl scale deployment/batcher --replicas=<current*1.25> -n prod`.
   - Step 4: Enable degraded-mode routing (route 10% of requests to cheaper read-only fallback model variant) via the routing control plane: `/bin/routingctl set-fallback inference-api 10%`.

3) Triage and restore (10-60 minutes):
   - Collect traces: `tempo query --service=inference-api --from="-15m"` and inspect trace latency distribution.
   - Check kv-cache metrics and backend model latencies.
   - If root cause is backend model (OOM, kernel crash), cordon affected nodes, drain, and restart: `kubectl cordon <node>`; `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
   - If traffic patterns are anomalous (spike from a single customer or route), apply request rate limiting for that API key: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/config/rate-limit -d '{"key":"<api_key>","qps":100}'`.

4) Recovery confirmation and close (after root cause fixed):
   - Verify SLO metrics returning to normal for two consecutive 30-minute windows.
   - Close PagerDuty incident with summary and link to postmortem.

Operational tooling and dashboards:

- Monitoring stack: Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), Tempo (tracing), Loki/ELK (logs), Alertmanager (alerts).
- Core dashboards required per service: SLO Summary, Error Budget Burn Rate, Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), Resource utilization (CPU/GPU/memory), Recent Deploys and Canary status.
- Alerts must map to SRE runbooks and be actionable (avoid high-noise alerts). Alert types:
  - Page: critical SLO breach, sustained burn_rate > 5, total service outage (>5 mins).
  - Ticket: elevated burn_rate (1 <= burn_rate <= 5), capacity nearing threshold (>= 80% of reserved pool).
  - Info: degraded latency under threshold but no customer impact.

- Integrations: PagerDuty for paging, Slack for incident channels and automation, GitHub for runbook and action-item tracking, JIRA for long-lived reliability initiatives.

Oncall model and rotations:

- Each service has a primary and secondary oncall. Oncall rotations are 1 week by default.
- Primary handles pages and immediate mitigation. Secondary assists and handles escalations and handoff.
- SRE manager maintains an oncall roster and ensures coverage for major holidays and planned engineering events.

Metrics and reporting:

- Weekly SLO health report published to the eng-sre space with: SLO attainment, error budget consumption, top incidents by budget impact, and open reliability initiatives.
- Monthly reliability review with product and platform stakeholders to align SLO targets, capacity plans, and roadmap priorities.

Change and review process:

- Changing an SLO requires a PR in infrastructure/slo-registry and approval from the service owner and SRE. Major target changes (>= 0.1% availability delta) must be discussed in the monthly reliability review.
- Runbooks must be reviewed quarterly by the service owner and SRE oncall and updated after any run that uses them.

Appendix: example alerts and Prometheus snippets

- SLO availability alert (critical):
  expr: (sum(increase(http_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\"}[30d])) - sum(increase(http_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\",status=~\"5..\"}[30d]))) / sum(increase(http_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\"}[30d])) < 0.9995
  for: 10m
  labels: severity=page
  annotations: runbook: https://confluence.internal/eng-sre/sre-slos-capacity-and-runbooks-guidelines-2026

- Burn rate alert (example):
  expr: increase(error_budget_seconds_burned_total{service=\"inference-api\"}[1h]) / (error_budget_seconds_total{service=\"inference-api\"} / 720) > 5
  for: 5m

- Contact points:
  - Primary oncall: inference-api rotation (PagerDuty)
  - SRE lead: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
  - Escalation: eng-sre@redwood.ai (Slack channel: #eng-sre-incidents)

Document maintenance and governance:

- Owner (engineering): SRE (Aisha Patel). This doc is the canonical standard for SRE operations at Redwood Inference.
- Review cadence: annual document review and after every Sev 1/2 incident.
- Where to store artifacts: runbooks in infrastructure/runbooks, SLO definitions in infrastructure/slo-registry, postmortems in incident-log repo.

If you have questions or need help onboarding an SLO for a service, contact the SRE team in #eng-sre or open an issue in the reliability-initiative board.
